- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates drop; add 1–2% to forecast to account for momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 2–3 days post-spike.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.33 to -0.33 in 2–3 days), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in cycle; apply 1–2% downward bias for first 10 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
